author: Ludendorff, Erich
title: My War Memories, 1914–1918 (Meine Kriegserinnerungen 1914–1918)
publisher: Hutchinson, London; E. S. Mittler, Berlin
notes: Ludendorff's memoir; the first-hand account of the 14th Brigade's night march into Liège and the surrender of the citadel on 7 August 1914. Self-serving on everything after; reliable for the Liège episode where the Reichsarchiv agrees. The citadel episode of 7 August — the white flags seen from La Chartreuse, the drive to the gate in a commandeered Belgian car, hammering on it, and the surrender of the few hundred Belgians inside — is at pp. 36–37; he gives no clock time for it. Volume II (archive.org item mywarmemories19102lude) carries the German reading of the tank battles: the surprise at Cambrai on 20 November 1917, and the sentence 'August 8th was the black day of the German Army in the history of this war.' Cited without pages, from the archive text.
